title: ‘Macbeth is destroyed as much by the influence of others as by his own desires.’ Discuss.
author: Dominic Salles
summary: Dominic Salles shares a practice Macbeth essay a student sent him for grading, which he recognised at once as AI-written because it is wordy, adjective-heavy, leans on the word ultimately and has too few quotations. He ran it through Gemini, which gave 26 out of 30 at the Grade 8 and 9 boundary, and through Tilf.io, a marker built around mark schemes and student answers, which gave 24 out of 30 with sharper feedback. His commentary is that the essay, at over 1200 words, would earn near full marks if real, yet no student will write like this in the exam. He agrees with all three of Tilf's even-better-if points: use more direct quotations, contextualise Lady Macbeth's role in Jacobean society, and tighten the conclusion, which he translates as stop waffling. He enjoys that AI can write a full-mark answer yet judge an AI essay as not quite good enough, and he notes that Tilf will not over-mark.
points: Tell-tale signs of an AI-written student essay include excess length, a fondness for adjectives and the word ultimately, and too few quotations.
Gemini and Tilf scored the same essay at 26 and 24 out of 30, and Salles prefers Tilf because its three improvement points apply to every future essay.
Feedback such as give an exact example is another way of saying quote, and Salles sees weak exam essays as using many words without reaching evidence.
He offers exam tactics: examiners will not penalise slightly inexact quotes, and writing about society more often raises marks.
The episode shows AI marking can act as a reality check, since a tool that produces a top-grade answer still grades an AI essay below the top.
quotes: It is obviously an AI essay - it is way too wordy, it is obsessed with adjectives and the word ‘ultimately’ and it doesn’t have enough quotes.
Obviously this would get a grade 9, and probably 30/30 in the real exam. But no student is going to write like this in the real exam.
My note - these strengths alone are typical of a full mark answer. Also, it is over 1200 words long which is another cast iron guarantee of full marks.
My note - this is exactly right. The essay uses loads of words without getting to a quote. This is no way to write an essay.
Give me an exact example is another way of saying: you need to quote!
I always teach students that the more often you write about society, the higher your mark.
But I very much like the idea that, although AI can write a full mark answer, it doesn’t think an essay written by AI is actually good enough.
The one thing I don’t like about Tilf is the one thing I don’t like about English teachers - it refuses to give full marks.
